extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO processing/examination staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for obtaining a filing date and proper processing of nonprovisional, provisional, design, continuation/divisional, and continued-prosecution patent applications, including fees, missing parts practice, informalities, and conversion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Date / Receipt Date stamping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office stamps papers and fees received through the mail (other than Priority Mail Express® under 37 CFR 1.10), by facsimile, or via the USPTO patent electronic filing system with the date of their receipt in the Office (the 'Office Date' stamp). Papers hand-carried to the Office are date stamped at the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the last day to take action or pay a fee falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C., the action/fee is timely if taken/paid on the next succeeding business day. Correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system is accorded a receipt date equal to the Eastern Time when received, regardless of weekends or Federal holidays. New applications filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 and deposited as Priority Mail Express® receive the USPS date of deposit (37 CFR 1.6(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date for nonprovisional applications (37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office for nonprovisional applications (except design/provisional special rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date. A continuing application may be filed under conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c) or 386(c) and § 1.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date for design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For design patents (except continued prosecution design applications under paragraph (d)), the filing date is the date on which the specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 (including at least one claim) and any required drawings are received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design application filing dates are subject to the same 'no new matter after filing' rule and to continued-prosecution-specific provisions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing requirements (37 CFR 1.53(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office; a provisional must include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1) (which may be an ADS or cover letter identifying it as provisional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment other than to make the provisional comply with the statute/regulations may be made after the provisional filing date. If a provisional lacks the cover sheet, it will be treated as a nonprovisional application under § 1.53(b). Provisional applications are not examined and become abandoned no later than 12 months after filing (35 U.S.C. 111(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a nonprovisional to provisional or provisional to nonprovisional is permitted under specified conditions and must be accompanied by the required processing/filing fees and, when converting to nonprovisional, an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b) unless already present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion to provisional does not entitle refund of fees paid. Conversion of a provisional to nonprovisional will cause the patent term to be measured from at least the provisional filing date; applicants are advised to consider claiming benefit of the provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) instead of conversion to avoid adverse patent term impact. Requests to convert must be filed prior to the earliest of: abandonment, payment of the issue fee, or expiration of 12 months after the provisional filing date; accompany required fees (§ 1.17(i)) and any required filing/search/examination fees and surcharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority and benefit limitations for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is not entitled to the right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 119, 365(a), or 386(a) or § 1.55, nor to the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) or § 1.78 of any other application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No claim for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or § 1.78(a) may be made in a design application based on a provisional application. Sequence data submissions in provisionals filed on or after July 1, 2022 must be by 'Sequence Listing XML' in compliance with §§ 1.831–1.834.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution (nonprovisional) / Continued prosecution application rules (37 CFR 1.53(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional (but not continuation-in-part) of a prior nonprovisional may be filed as a continued prosecution application under paragraph (d) if certain conditions are met (e.g., design applications; prior application complete as defined; filed before payment of issue fee, abandonment, or termination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date of a continued prosecution application is the date a request on a separate paper is filed. The application must identify the prior application, disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application, name the same inventors (with limited exceptions), include the request and use the prior application's file jacket and contents, be assigned the prior application's application number, and expressly abandon the prior application as of the filing date of the request. Filing fees for continued prosecution applications are the basic filing, search, and examination fees as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship requirements for continuation/divisional vs continuation-in-part
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application may name the same or fewer inventors than in the prior application; a continuation-in-part or continuation/divisional naming an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under the paragraph permitting new matter (i.e., different paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed under continued-prosecution paragraph may be filed by fewer than all inventors if accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the non-inventors; no person may be named who was not named in the prior application except via correction under § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in continued prosecution applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new change in a continued prosecution application must be made by amendment to the prior application as it existed before filing; no amendment in a continued prosecution application may introduce new matter or matter that would have been new matter in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new specification filed with the request will be treated as a substitute specification in accordance with § 1.125 and will not be considered part of the original application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of confidentiality for continued prosecution applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a continued prosecution application is construed to include a waiver of confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent that members of the public entitled under § 1.14 to access information on the prior application may be given similar access to the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access provisions apply to the prior and continuing application file jackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet filing date requirements — notice and correction period
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application deposited under paragraphs (b), (c), or (d) does not meet the requirements to be entitled to a filing date, the applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given time to correct the filing error; otherwise the filing date will be the date the filing error is corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for review of such notification must be by petition accompanied by the fee (§ 1.17(f)). If the applicant fails to correct within time, proceedings may be terminated and application disposed of; filing fees less handling fee (§ 1.21(n)) may be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of application after filing — fees and missing parts treatment (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application that has been accorded a filing date lacks required fees (basic filing, search, or examination), at least one claim, or inventor's oath/declaration, and a correspondence address is provided, the applicant will be notified and given time to pay and/or submit the missing items to avoid abandonment; if no correspondence address provided, applicant has three months from filing date to provide them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventor's oath/declaration may be postponed until the application is in condition for allowance if an ADS meeting § 1.76 conditions is filed identifying each inventor by legal name and mailing/residence addresses. Filing late fees may trigger surcharges (§ 1.16(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims, multiple dependent claim fees, and application size fee timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees (§ 1.16(h),(i)) or multiple dependent claim fee (§ 1.16(j)) or application size fee (§ 1.16(s)) are not paid on filing or on later presentation, the required fees must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application size fee applies for each additional 50 sheets (or fraction) over 100; calculation excludes compliant Sequence Listing CRF/XML and Computer Program Listing Appendix files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of nonpayment of basic filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not pay the basic filing fee during the pendency of the application, the Office may dispose of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposition may include abandonment and refund only as provided (less handling fees) under applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of provisional applications lacking required parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If provisional papers do not include at least a specification containing a description (and drawings if necessary) or are too informal to be given a filing date, the case is held in OPAP as incomplete and applicant is informed; no filing date is granted until corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component parts necessary for provisional filing date include: specification (per 35 U.S.C. 112(a) / pre-AIA 112 first paragraph and 37 CFR 1.71) and drawings if necessary (37 CFR 1.81(a) for applications before March 18, 2013). A provisional lacking a cover sheet is treated as a nonprovisional under § 1.53(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal application definition and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is informal if typed on both sides, not permanent, not legible, or not reproducible. If such informalities are timely corrected, the application is given the filing date on which the original informal papers were filed; failure to correct results in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will send a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers requiring correction of the informality; the filing date is accorded as of the 'Office Date' stamp when required components are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing parts practice for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 contains applicable filing fees (basic, search, examination), the surcharge (§ 1.16(f)), and a signed ADS providing required inventor information but lacks the inventor's oath/declaration, the Office will not issue a Notice to File Missing Parts requiring the oath; instead it may send an informational notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application also lacks applicable filing fees, the surcharge, or a signed ADS, the Office will issue a Notice To File Missing Parts giving a time period (usually two months) to file the missing items to avoid abandonment. If in condition for allowance and oath not filed, Notice of Allowability will require oath/declaration no later than payment of issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing / Computer Program Listing exclusions from application size fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Sequence Listing or CRF of a Sequence Listing in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821(c)/(e), any Sequence Listing XML in compliance with 37 CFR 1.831(a), and any Computer Program Listing Appendix in compliance with 37 CFR 1.96(c) submitted on read-only optical disc or via the electronic filing system will be excluded when determining the application size fee under 37 CFR 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.52(f) and MPEP § 607 for additional fee calculation details. The application size fee must be paid prior to the expiration of the time set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments canceling claims — requirements and advice
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) may be filed with a preliminary amendment limited to cancellation of claims, but any preliminary amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (include complete listing of all claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office recommends filing applications with the desired set of claims rather than filing with a preliminary amendment canceling claims. A preliminary amendment cancelling claims diminishes the number of claims considered for filing fee calculation. No refund will be made once claim fees are properly paid even if claims are later canceled, unless a petition for express abandonment under 37 CFR 1.138(d) is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date and review of claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A filing date is normally granted before review of the subject matter claimed in a nonprovisional application; if the application appears sufficient, it is forwarded to the examiner for consideration in the regular course of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents purporting to be a specification are so incoherent that they do not constitute a specification per 35 U.S.C. 112 and 37 CFR 1.71, the application will not be accorded a filing date until corrections are made (filing date becomes date corrections are made).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of refusal to accord filing date (petition process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any review of a refusal to grant a filing date as of the date of deposit of the application is by petition accompanied by the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner should provide arguments that the noted items were not missing or that a filing date should be assigned absent such items, and may request refund of the petition fee if alleging no defect exists. Petitions should include supporting arguments/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date treatment when some components are received after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If any required items are missing when filed, the applicant will be notified to file them and the filing date will be the date of receipt of the missing part(s); a supplemental oath/declaration may be required in certain circumstances for older filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, an error in or failure to identify inventorship does not raise a filing date issue. Supplemental declarations may be needed where parts are missing for applications filed before Sept 16, 2012.
